name: Mega Menu
summary: Non-modal site-navigation disclosure with labelled native link groups, optional promotional and featured destinations, controlled visibility, ordinary link keyboard behavior, container response, and target-owned trigger policy.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: Labelled non-modal site-navigation disclosure controlled by an external target-owned Button.

anatomy.name: column
anatomy.description: Optional navigation group labelled by its visible heading.

anatomy.name: list
anatomy.description: Native list of destinations in one labelled group.

anatomy.name: listItem
anatomy.description: Native list item containing one destination link.

anatomy.name: link
anatomy.description: Native site destination link with optional current-page state.

anatomy.name: promo
anatomy.description: Optional single promotional destination link whose visible text supplies its name.

anatomy.name: featured
anatomy.description: Labelled native featured-destination list and responsive grid.

variants.name: promo
variants.description: Mega menu composition that includes promotional media blocks.

variants.name: featured
variants.description: Mega menu composition that includes a featured item grid.

states.name: linkHover
states.description: Fine-pointer hover state on ordinary destination links. Variant-specific selectors are implementation coverage of this same state.

states.name: linkFocus
states.description: Visible keyboard focus on every destination type.

states.name: currentPage
states.description: Actual current destination with non-color text emphasis.

behavior.name: openState
behavior.description: Controlled open state synchronizes visual visibility, pointer availability, immediate descendant focus availability, and accessibility-tree exposure.

behavior.name: siteNavigation
behavior.description: Groups use native lists and ordinary links with normal document Tab order; menu/menubar roles, roving focus, arrow navigation, and focus trapping are not used.

behavior.name: disclosureController
behavior.description: An external target-owned Button controls the surface and owns activation, dismissal, focus restoration when moved, pointer intent, and mobile substitution.

behavior.name: promoNavigation
behavior.description: A promo is one native destination link named by visible text; decorative media uses an empty alternative.

behavior.name: featuredNavigation
behavior.description: Featured destinations form a labelled native list of ordinary links.

behavior.name: responsiveContainment
behavior.description: The surface evaluates narrow layouts against its own inline size, preserves bounded block scrolling, and never creates page inline overflow.

behavior.name: motionAndContrast
behavior.description: Reduced motion removes layer/media transforms and forced colors restores system surface, link, current, focus, and promo contrast.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Accessible name for the mega-menu navigation region.

properties.name: open
properties.description: Controls visible and accessible hidden state. The target remains the only controlled owner of trigger relationships, activation, dismissal, and restoration.

properties.name: columns
properties.description: Optional target-owned visible-heading-labelled groups with native lists and destination links.

properties.name: promo
properties.description: Optional single promotional destination link with visible naming and normally decorative media.

properties.name: featured
properties.description: Optional target-owned labelled native list of featured destination links and media.

accessibility: Expose the surface as a clearly labelled native navigation landmark with visible-heading-labelled native destination lists.
Synchronize aria-hidden, inert, and visual state with an external Button's aria-expanded and aria-controls relationship.
Keep ordinary Link Tab and activation behavior; do not use application-menu roles, roving focus, arrow-key navigation, or a focus trap.
Keep closed descendants out of focus and accessibility APIs; target adapters provide Escape/intentional dismissal and restore focus when they moved it.
Use visible text to name promo and featured links, avoid duplicate image alternatives, and mark only the actual current destination with aria-current=page.
Preserve visible focus, logical geometry, reduced motion, forced colors, and bounded localized content.

web.notes: Canonical CSS provides controlled presentation, native grouped-link structure, container response, focus/current/special-media states, and no neutral runtime; target code owns the disclosure controller.

shopify.notes: Liquid should map menu/linklist and promo/featured blocks while target JavaScript owns the external Button lifecycle, route state, dismissal, and mobile substitution.
